defect: The new C# default candidate-file routing reduces each source file to one namespace via namespace_of_file, then admits unqualified type references only against that namespace. A valid reference under a later namespace block in the same file is omitted when its declaration is in another file, so the usage scanner never sees that reference.
fact: `CSharpAnalyzer::namespace_of_file` (src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:150-160) collapses a source file to only its first non-empty declaration namespace via `.find(...)`, and `CSharpAnalyzer::referencing_files_of` (src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:284-308) admits bare type references in a candidate file only when that single namespace matches `target_namespaces`.
other_facts: `CSharpAdapter::parse_file` (src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:62-77) initializes `ParsedFile` with an empty file-level package (line 68) while `CSharpVisitor::visit_namespace` (src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:671-687) assigns per-block namespaces to declarations.

`ImportGraphCandidateProvider::find_candidates` (src/usages/candidates.rs:83-90) populates cross-directory `candidate_files` from `referencing_files_of`, and `CSharpUsageGraphStrategy::find_usages` (src/usages/csharp_graph.rs:66-90) scans only `candidate_files` plus `target.source()`.
evidence: At intro 88fa9bb729af44cc316e5b18c68ca7443cfb25c5, the diff itself adds `namespace_of_file` returning one `String` from `.find(|package| !package.is_empty())` (src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:150-160), adds `referencing_files_of` which collects a `HashSet<String>` of `target_namespaces` for the target file (lines 259-264) yet compares each candidate against `let candidate_namespace = self.namespace_of_file(candidate)` (lines 291-301), adds `CSharpUsageGraphStrategy::find_usages` scanning only `candidate_files` plus `target.source()` (src/usages/csharp_graph.rs:66-86), and adds `usage_finder_csharp_candidate_routing_covers_using_and_same_namespace` (tests/usages_csharp_graph_test.rs:1034-1094) showing `UsageFinder::new().query` pruning `candidate_files` through that provider.

defect: The new JavaScript object-literal declaration walker labels every property CodeUnitType::Field, including method_definition nodes and function-valued properties. Consequently a real object method is absent from the function results returned by search_symbols and is exposed with the wrong symbol kind.
fact: `visit_js_object_literal_properties` (src/analyzer/javascript/mod.rs:929-959) unconditionally constructs `CodeUnit::new(..., CodeUnitType::Field, ...)` (lines 944-949) for every node matched by `js_object_literal_property_name` (src/analyzer/javascript/mod.rs:961-979), even though `js_object_literal_property_name` explicitly accepts `method_definition` (line 967) and function-valued `pair` nodes (lines 963-965).
other_facts: `search_symbols` (src/searchtools.rs:655-669) partitions file results into `functions` (`CodeUnitType::Function`, line 664) and `fields` (`CodeUnitType::Field`, line 665).
evidence: At intro fe862359a21a9f7ce9b72ecf2e8dc1481d191f6f, the diff in src/analyzer/javascript/mod.rs:904-979 shows `visit_js_variable_statement` branching on `is_function` in context (lines 909-920), then adds `visit_js_object_literal_properties` hardcoding `CodeUnitType::Field` (lines 944-949) alongside `js_object_literal_property_name` explicitly matching `"method_definition"` (line 967) and `"pair"` (line 963). While `CodeUnitType::Function` assignment (src/analyzer/javascript/mod.rs:799, 877) and `search_symbols` bucketing (src/searchtools.rs:664-665) lie outside the diff, misclassifying `method_definition` and function-valued properties as `CodeUnitType::Field` is directly visible in the added walker.

defect: The new Kotlin value-class carrier classification handles bound names and constructions but omits this_expression and never binds the procedure receiver to its enclosing value class. Consequently a member reading this.amount from its own same-file value class misses the underlying-value projection and is lowered as a generic field load with a field-identity gap, losing the carrier dependence that the new value-class semantics can prove.
fact: `LoweringContext::expression_carrier` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/kotlin/semantic/values.rs:518-528) matches only `simple_identifier` and `call_expression`, returning `KotlinCarrier::Unrelated` for `this_expression`, and `lower_procedure` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/kotlin/semantic/control.rs:39-64) never binds `self.receiver` to an enclosing value class in `self.carriers`.
other_facts: `LoweringContext::emit_procedure_inputs` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/kotlin/semantic/values.rs:268-284) allocates `self.receiver` as `SemanticValueKind::Receiver { dispatch: true }` for non-static member procedures without inserting into `self.carriers`, and `emit_lexical_input_flow` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/kotlin/semantic/values.rs:316-321) resolves `this_expression` from `self.captured_receiver` or `self.receiver`.

When `underlying_projection` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/kotlin/semantic/values.rs:685-695) returns `None`, `property_load` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/kotlin/semantic/control.rs:1976-1993) falls back to `MemoryLocationKind::Field`, `add_field_identity_gap`, and `SemanticEffect::MemoryLoad`.
evidence: At intro ba47ae3f428ea3e1d51d999176397a21ea71bff5, the diff introduces `carriers: HashMap<ValueId, KotlinCarrier>` right above `receiver: Option<ValueId>` and `captured_receiver: Option<ValueId>` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/kotlin/semantic/mod.rs:357-368; control.rs:48-55), populates `carriers` only via `bind_carrier` on locals and formal parameters (values.rs:144, 241; control.rs:850), defines `expression_carrier` handling only `"simple_identifier"` and `"call_expression"` (values.rs:518-528), and wires `property_load` (control.rs:1964-1978) to check `underlying_projection` (values.rs:685-695) before falling through to `MemoryLocationKind::Field`.

defect: The new model-overload selector records conversion failures in a failures list but returns its sole successful candidate without consulting that list. A competing model signature whose parameter identity or conversion is unknown is therefore silently discarded as though proven incompatible, and the public call-binding result can report proven conversions to an unjustifiably selected overload.
fact: `CallConversionCache::select_model_signature` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/usages/call_conversion.rs:806-844) pushes `ConversionUnknown` errors from competing model candidates into `failures` (lines 812, 817, 828) yet returns `Ok(Some((model_id.clone(), signature.clone())))` unconditionally when `applicable` has one element (line 838).
other_facts: `JavaCallArgumentConversionProver::prove_model_argument` and `resolve_model_type_ref` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/java/call_conversion.rs:134-152, 396-456) return `Err(ConversionUnknown::UnresolvedTargetType | GenericSubstitution | AmbiguousBinding | UnsupportedConversion)` when a formal parameter's type or conversion cannot be resolved.

`model_call_binding` and `call_binding_expansions` (crates/bifrost-rql/src/structural/search/call_binding.rs:490-526, 1000-1025, 1123-1132) turn `Ok(Some(...))` from `select_model_signature` into `ModelCallBinding::Unique` and populate conversion rows for that selected signature.
evidence: At intro 2dc7a9b231a028ebd9412c5241b90beea841c589, every part of the defect is introduced directly in the diff: `select_model_signature` (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/usages/call_conversion.rs:806-844) records `failures` for unresolved/unsupported competitors and ignores `failures` on the singleton `[(model_id, signature)]` match arm at line 838; the same diff adds `prove_model_argument` returning `Err(ConversionUnknown::...)` for unresolved or unsupported model `TypeRef`s (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/java/call_conversion.rs:134-152, 396-456) and wires `select_model_signature` into `ModelCallBinding::Unique` and `populate_conversions` (crates/bifrost-rql/src/structural/search/call_binding.rs:490-526, 1123-1132).

defect: The return-type reader now strips Option<T> to T without requiring an unwrap operation. An ordinary call returning Option<T> is inferred as the payload, so a subsequent bare field read can navigate to a field of T even though the receiver is still an Option.
fact: `rust_function_return_type_text` (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:1045-1055) unconditionally strips `Option<T>` to `T` via `rust_unwrap_container_type` (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:1057-1075), while `.expect`/`.unwrap` in `rust_value_type_fqn` (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:984-994) merely delegates to `rust_expression_type_fqn` on the bare receiver.
other_facts: `rust_callable_return_type` (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:1030-1043) passes every callable signature through `rust_function_return_type_text` (line 1041), which `rust_value_type_fqn` invokes for ordinary calls (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:1012-1016).

`rust_collect_binding_type_fqn` (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:896-918) infers untyped `let` bindings from `rust_value_type_fqn` (lines 911-916), and `resolve_rust_field` (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:588-619) resolves bare field accesses from that inferred owner.
evidence: At intro 309939da522fa0c3cf51ec922c15c1f5f81ff31a, `git show 309939da522fa0c3cf51ec922c15c1f5f81ff31a` directly contains `rust_function_return_type_text` and `rust_unwrap_container_type` stripping `Option<` and `std::option::Option<` unconditionally (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:1051-1063), `rust_value_type_fqn` handling `expect | unwrap` by returning `rust_expression_type_fqn(..., receiver, ...)` unchanged and inferring ordinary calls via `rust_callable_return_type` (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:984-1016), `resolve_rust_field` querying `rust_expression_type_fqn` on the field receiver (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:595-606), and the new test in tests/get_definition_test.rs:233 where `pricing() -> Option<RouteCheapnessEstimate>` with `.expect(...)` resolves `fast.input_price_per_mtok_micros` even though `.expect(...)` added no unwrap step.
